summary: Our project was both a physical representation and a game. The objective of the challenge was toto create an intuitive tool or application that lets mission planners, educators, and the public compare landing sites and dates quickly, visualizing Sun and Earth positions relative to the horizon to assess power generation potential and direct-to-Earth. Our project helps meet this objective because, the physical representation allows all the above stakeholders to visualise and compare multiple landing sites, while also visualising the positions of the sun, and earth relative to the horizon.  The game allows the stakeholders to type in their preferred landing sites, type of spacecraft, time and date, position, and other information's. The game will then provide them with the best landing site option, with details about the chosen landing site at that specific chosen date and time.  The game also gives the player the chance to control how the spacecraft moves and lands on that specific time. If the spacecraft falls, or destroys it means that landing spot wasn't really feasible, with that spacecraft.
details:
Physical Representation

Our actual solution, regarding the physical representation. It will be a system with a representation of the sun, earth, and the moon. The moon and the earth constantly rotate, there will be a screen to display the date and the time, the user can change the time and the date, to see the position of the earth and sun at a specific landing spot at a certain time. Then the user scans the QR code, and the person will be given a set of options to pick, such as the space craft type, landing site, etc. After the person picks, the game will give the user the best landing site out the options, and then it will give the user the opportunity to control the spacecraft and land the spacecraft. If the spacecraft falls or destroys, then it will mean that the chosen landing spot or the date and time, or the spacecraft chosen, or how the user landed the spacecraft, was not feasible with the land site.

For our prototype of the physical solution, we created a moon, and printed the sun and the earth, and we marked some spots on the moon (the top, bottom, and the sides) and then we pasted the QR code of the game near the moon, so the user picks a marked spot, scans the QR code and then play the game.

The Game

SELENE is an interactive lunar landing simulator that combines NASA terrain data, JPL ephemerides, three-dimensional Moon visualization, spacecraft design, and machine learning. Players can build a lander, choose launch time, sunlight conditions, starting latitude, longitude, and altitude, then navigate manually or automatically toward destinations anywhere on the Moon. The system evaluates terrain slope, lighting, Earth visibility, spacecraft performance, fuel, battery, and landing dynamics to recommend the best landing site. Users can inspect success probabilities, launch from orbit, follow routes, and perform realistic, guided descents. SELENE transforms lunar mission planning into an accessible educational game for exploration, engineering, and data-driven decision-making.

How our work is creative

It was the only solution with a physical representation. We also used recycled products to make the product such as balloons, tree branch, paper, cardboard, and a paper bag.
